01.words: Fellow Americans, Florida sent me here hopeful, and I mean to stay that way. Across the generations, this country has faced hard questions like grocery inflation before, and each generation has had to answer them in its turn. // The gains on higher pay give this country room to hope. This oath binds me to Florida and to every other state alike.

06.words:
First thing on January 30th, Isaiah Calderon stops by while you work.
Isaiah Calderon can't let go of a higher minimum wage, and the story in Meridian News Network is the reason. // Isaiah Calderon: Fair warning: I read the whole thing in Meridian News Network on a higher minimum wage, and now I have opinions. [Replies: I read it too. I didn't love it, but it's fair. | It sounded like somebody who has never had to live with it. | I didn't see it. What did it say? | Can we do this later? I'm not up for the news right now.] // Isaiah Calderon: BLAIR OLSON
I read it too. I didn't love it, but it's fair.
Does that mean you'd say something, if someone asked? [Replies: Yeah. I think it does matter. I just didn't want to say so. | We can both read it and not agree. | Let me read it again before I say anything else.] // Isaiah Calderon: BLAIR OLSON
Yeah. I think it does matter. I just didn't want to say so.
So why isn't anyone doing anything about a higher minimum wage? We're the ones who live with it. [Replies: All right, you're right. It bothers me too. | I saw it. They only told one side of a higher minimum wage, and that's the side people will remember. | I'm sorry. I can't get into this right now.] // Isaiah Calderon: BLAIR OLSON
All right, you're right. It bothers me too.
Then what do we do about it? [Replies: I read it twice. I still don't buy it. | I'll think about it. I have to go.] // Isaiah Calderon: BLAIR OLSON
I read it twice. I still don't buy it.
Really? Read it again, then.
I'll probably bring it up again once I've read more.

08.words:
Susan Griffin: First thing on October 30th, you step into the Secretary of State's office and ask for Susan Griffin. // Susan Griffin: Can I help you? [Replies: I want to run for U.S. Senator. November 3, 2026 · Held by Allison Craig | I want to run for U.S. Representative (District 4). November 3, 2026 · Held by Jessica Rivera] // Susan Griffin: BLAIR OLSON
I want to run for U.S. Senator.
Running for U.S. Senator? Good. Let me pull the papers. You'd serve 6 years. First comes the primary, March 10, 2026, and then the general, November 3, 2026. It's a statewide office. Every voter in the state gets a say in who holds it. The papers are due back December 26.
You have to be at least 30. [Replies: Alright.]
